references.text: In both cases, the question of becoming disciples is used as a rhetorical attack against those who testify about Jesus. In John 9:34, the Pharisees call the healed man a sinner, while in John 9:27 he ironically asks if they too want to become his disciples.

The theme of fear of excommunication (being cast out of the synagogue) is central throughout the entire chapter. In John 9:22, the parents fear this, while in John 9:27 the son challenges the Pharisees with precisely this consequence of becoming disciples.

The contrast between seeing and being blind is a recurring motif. In John 9:27, the healed man ironically asks if the Pharisees want to become disciples, which leads directly to the conclusion in John 9:40-41 that their blindness is a moral condition.

The direct dialogue about becoming disciples in John 9:27 prepares for the meeting between Jesus and the healed man in John 9:35-38, where the healed man actually becomes a disciple by believing in the Son of Man.
